method: Literal question and answer-rationale review across the complete 240-entry records. Targeted fresh primary-source reading concentrated on restored answers and questionable older inferences. Existing unknown entries remain unresolved; this review does not claim exhaustive new research on every unknown. Source absence was not encoded as zero. Scores were not consulted.
sourceReadChecks: Liberal International Andorra 2017 and marriage reform 2002, indexed full text; 2012 LGBTI principles considered with the stated equality inference.
TRG King’s Speech 6 November 2023 and Hong Kong BNO campaign 28 May 2020, full indexed text.
Hobhouse Social Evolution and Political Theory: social transmission, inherited capacities, and the distinction between social and racial progress; modest Culture/Nature inferences retained.
US AI Action Plan July 2025: workforce displacement provisions retained; environmental permitting did not establish the two habitat/uncertainty tradeoffs.
Kristol 1983 interview and 2003 Neoconservative Persuasion: mixed redistribution/planning retained; alternative delivery does not establish private contractor preference.
National Conservatism 2022 principles, all ten sections: religious public morality and federal exceptions retained; deterrence distinguished from supremacy and an exclusive armed-attack rule.
Duniam 21 July 2026 immigration speech: housing ceiling, temporary status and common civic obligations retained as opposition programme, not incumbent acts.

Thatcher 1979 manifesto, Right Approach, UN environmental speech and 1988 Christianity speech: immigration temporary-settlement rule and national core curriculum retained; tax-band differentiation directly contradicts inferred flat marginal rates.

NOW Issues Manual: CAFTA pp89–92, progressive taxation p194, welfare pp44–46, national rights floor p196, local CEDAW and health campaigns, religion/church-state sections; adopted 2021 foreign-policy and draft abolition resolutions; 2007 immigration principles; SEP liberal feminism autonomy, sex education and gradualism passages.
limitations: Review completion is not assessment completion. No revision was archived, no catalogue was regenerated and no percentages were restored.

profiles.scope: International constitutional liberalism in Liberal International’s Oxford (1947) and Andorra (2017) manifestos. Andorra explicitly renews Oxford; it supplies contemporary positions rather than projecting 1947 silence onto modern questions. This is the federation’s agreed doctrine, not every member government’s conduct. Unsupported empirical causal comparisons remain unresolved.

changes.question: My country’s national identity should include several distinct cultural ways of life.

before.rationale: The vision expressly embraces diverse identities and backgrounds.

after.rationale: Unresolved after independent source review: Embracing diverse personal identities does not expressly settle incorporating multiple traditions into the official national identity.

changes.question: Families outside the traditional two-parent married household should receive the same social recognition as that household.

before.rationale: The marriage resolution rejects inadequate recognition of families outside existing marriage rules.

after.rationale: The marriage resolution challenges exclusion of nonconforming families and outmoded constraints. This supports a qualified inference towards equal social recognition; legal status is more directly evidenced than identical social recognition.

changes.question: Society should continue to favour the two-parent married household as its preferred family model.

before.rationale: The resolution values parental commitment while rejecting exclusion of nonconforming families, qualifying preference for one family form.

after.rationale: Unresolved after independent source review: Legal recognition of nonconforming families and parental commitment do not settle whether society should favour the married two-parent model.

changes.question: People fleeing persecution should be allowed to enter and receive protection even when ordinary immigration limits have been reached.

before.rationale: The Hong Kong campaign supports refuge from persecution despite the government’s ordinary migration restrictions; this is a qualified humanitarian exception, not unrestricted immigration.

after.rationale: Unresolved after independent source review: The Hong Kong BNO proposal concerns a specific historic legal responsibility. It does not establish the general refugee-admission rule when ordinary immigration limits have been reached.

changes.question: My country should prioritise technological solutions to climate change over reducing energy and material consumption, even when those technologies are not yet proven at large scale.

before.rationale: TRG advocates emerging direct-air-capture technology financed by fossil-fuel producers.

after.rationale: Unresolved after independent source review: Support for carbon capture alongside net zero does not establish giving unproven technology priority over reducing energy and material consumption.

changes.question: My country should prioritise expanding housing and transport infrastructure over preserving undeveloped land when the two conflict.

before.rationale: TRG prioritises additional homes and planning reform; environmental commitments qualify the preference.

after.rationale: Unresolved after independent source review: More homes and planning reform do not establish preferring development of undeveloped land over preservation; the source does not identify the land or this trade-off.

profiles.scope: American neoconservatism as synthesised by Irving Kristol (1983–2003), including post-Cold War American primacy and democracy promotion associated with PNAC. Neither every member of an administration nor every later conservative is represented.

changes.question: My country should restrict imports from foreign firms that receive large subsidies from their governments.

before.rationale: The economic strategy permits targeted action against damaging foreign dumping.

after.rationale: Unresolved after independent source review: Action against dumping is not identical to restricting imports from firms receiving large government subsidies. The cited passage does not settle that distinct criterion.

changes.question: Additional income earned by high earners should not face higher tax rates than additional income earned by other workers.

before.rationale: Lower marginal-rate differences support productive effort.

after.rationale: The 1979 manifesto explicitly proposes cutting the top rate and widening higher bands while retaining a differentiated income-tax structure. This supports qualified disagreement with identical marginal rates; lower top rates do not imply a flat rate.

sourceIssues: Some Liberal International/TRG pages failed direct opening; indexed full-page text was read instead where available. No numeric answer was accepted on an inaccessible URL alone.
